title: Should i use my DEMO to promote my game?
author: BBmanse
selftext:
Ive been developing a game for the last 4 months. I want to eventually launch it, im wondering if launching a demo of it so people can tell me feedback would be a good way to understand how much it can land into players. 

Everyone thinks their game is great like a parent that loves his kids.

Also maybe the demo could be a decent way to start marketing and maybe get some people interested in the wishlist.

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: Hasn’t this been the purpose of demos since the 80s?

replies.author: BBmanse
replies.body: Should i worry about the risk of someone copying my game based on the demo i upload?

replies.author: Three_Tails_Studio
replies.body: That has also been an issue since the dawn of time. If your game is good it will inspire others, if it’s not, no one will care.

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body:
yes, you should.  however, once your demo launches, you have successfully beachheadded the idea.  you'll be fine unless the copycat is someone who can throw hundreds of thousands of dollars at advertising.

so if you're making wow or something extremely viral, be worried about the demo too.  if it's a regular indie game, just make your game and don't worry too much about it.

replies.author: Comet7777
replies.body: If your demo is successful, you’ll be fine

replies.author: Weaves87
replies.body:
Make sure that your demo is a different build that doesn't include all of your game's content (e.g. don't include all levels). Ask Claude how you can set something like this up and he will guide you

If your demo is getting copied then you are doing something right. Just make sure you don't include all of the content (so someone can't generate a complete ripoff). If they can only straight up rip 5 level designs from your game, then they'll have to come up with the rest of the content on their own, and most of these losers copying games won't bother with that (or just straight up aren't capable)

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body: Assuming you mean Steam, yes, that's currently the preferred strategy

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body: oh what the fuck is this garbage

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body:

it also got the counting wrong.  i'm one syllable short of 5-7-5 and to get to 5-7-4 you have to split words.  a highschool student submitting this as homework would fail.

there also already are dozens of these.  i've opted out of so much of this dreary, uninteresting chaff, but here comes some douchebag to clone an existing bad idea, instead of doing something new.

comments.author: Moist_Signal_5080
comments.body: Just be careful that you don’t have a simple on/off flag for the demo. I know Claude likes to do that by default if you ask if to make the demo. Make sure it’s a separate build, so people can access the whole game.

replies.author: BBmanse
replies.body: Actually. I dont think the game will be 100% ready by the time i upload the demo, im actually expecting to use some feed back to code back some improvements.

replies.author: Captain_Slib
replies.body: So is it a demo or an alpha test?

replies.author: BBmanse
replies.body: Excuse my ignorance, but in order to upload a demo you need to have the game fully finished? 😅

replies.author: Captain_Slib
replies.body: Youre the one asking if a DEMO should be used for MARKETING your game, dude... like what are we doing here??

replies.author: TheVoidCookingBeans
replies.body: He was asking if a demo requires the game to.be finished, he is learning, don't be a dick

replies.author: TheVoidCookingBeans
replies.body: A demo should be a taste of the final product, so yes. An alpha test is essentially a demo of the unfinished game, so thing stay subject to change.

replies.author: BBmanse
replies.body: Thanks man. Thats more clear to me now

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: The route I’m going is steam page, trailer, demo. In that order.

comments.author: KittyD172
comments.body: I use Itch.io for the feedback. Some of the game jams are very good for this.

comments.author: Forward_Key_4937
comments.body: Yes, the demo, which will be on Steam for a few weeks, will help you. Besides, wait for a Steam fest, it gives you more opportunities to play. I recommend it.

comments.author: kmrodrigo
comments.body:
A demo eh necessária para encontrar problemas e melhorias, pra você ter uma ideia divulgando apenas o vídeo em comunidades recebi diversos feedbacks que me ajudaram a melhorar (mesmo dos haters) 

No entanto a demo também vai fazer a galera da wishlist testar, se for muito ruim vai perder, tente compartilhar com amigos primeiro

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
you don't have to release a demo if you don't want. if you can get enough attention without a demo, then it doesn't matter. 

having a demo should in theory help with the conversion rate especially if your game has a higher price point.

just pay attention to the traffic stats and act accordingly I guess. 

if you are not getting views and clicks, may as well make a demo
